gold.text: The participants introduced their roles: project manager, user interface designer, industrial designer, and marketing expert.
The project manager asked Ed, the marketing expert, for a marketing/product plan; Ed said the team needed to develop it together and agreed to provide a plan by the next meeting.
After initial confusion about the product, the team clarified that it was designing a television remote control and discussed a fresh, attractive, user-friendly design.

The project manager requested a written initial functional/technical design plan from the industrial designer, including staffing, timing and budget, and asked the marketing expert to coordinate on sales and costs.
The marketing expert discussed competitor research, identifying a target market, and combining an attractive new design with simplicity of use.
The user interface designer described her usability-requirement work and collaboration with the industrial designer; the team agreed to keep the marketing expert and project manager informed.
The immediate next step was functional design, informed by usability and marketing, with further discussion at the next meeting.
The marketing expert will prepare a sales/project plan, coordinating costs and marketing strategy with the industrial designer.
The industrial designer will prepare an initial written functional/technical design plan, including staffing, timing and budget, in consultation with marketing.
The user interface designer will study usability/user requirements and work with the industrial designer on user acceptability and testing, keeping marketing informed.
The project manager will send the participants a copy of his presentation slides at the conclusion of this meeting.
gold.deadline: at the conclusion of our meeting
